extracted.subtask_description: Administrative and procedural requirements for U.S. patent prosecution, including micro entity fee eligibility, power of attorney, correspondence, representation, revocation/withdrawal, and inventorship rules. Focused on what must be certified, signed, filed, and who may act or receive correspondence in an application or patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro entity certification — general requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish micro entity status an applicant must certify entitlement in writing complying with paragraph (a) or (d) of § 1.29 and sign in compliance with signature rules (e.g., § 1.33(b)). Status must be specifically established in each related, continuing and reissue application in which status is appropriate and desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status as a micro entity in one application or patent does not affect the status of any other application or patent. Refiling as a continuation, divisional, continuation-in-part, or filing a reissue requires a new certification for the continuing or reissue application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro entity criterion (a)(1) — small entity qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must qualify as a small entity as defined in § 1.27 without relying on a government use license exception under § 1.27(a)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a prerequisite for micro entity certification under paragraph (a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro entity criterion (a)(2) — prior applications limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither the applicant nor the inventor nor a joint inventor has been named as the inventor or a joint inventor on more than four previously filed patent applications, other than applications filed in another country, provisional applications under 35 U.S.C. 111(b), or international applications for which the basic national fee under 35 U.S.C. 41(a) was not paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (b) provides an exception where an applicant/inventor is not considered named on a previously filed application if all ownership rights were assigned due to the inventor’s previous employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro entity criterion (a)(3) — gross income threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: In the calendar year preceding the year the fee is paid, neither the applicant nor the inventor nor a joint inventor had a gross income (per 26 U.S.C. 61(a)) exceeding three times the median household income for that preceding calendar year as most recently reported by the Bureau of the Census.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If gross income is not in U.S. dollars, use the IRS average currency exchange rate for that year to determine whether the threshold is exceeded (see paragraph (c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro entity criterion (a)(4) — assignment/license to high-income entity
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither the applicant nor the inventor nor a joint inventor has assigned, granted, or conveyed, nor is under an obligation to assign/grant/convey, a license or other ownership interest in the application to an entity that in the preceding calendar year had gross income exceeding three times the median household income for that preceding calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such assignment/obligation exists to an entity above the income threshold the micro entity criterion is not met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro entity alternative qualification (d) — institution of higher education path
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish micro entity status under paragraph (d), the applicant must: (1) qualify as a small entity under § 1.27 (without relying on a government use exception), and (2)(i) obtain the majority of income from an institution of higher education as defined in the Higher Education Act, or (ii) have assigned/granted/ conveyed (or be under an obligation to do so) a license or other ownership interest in the particular application to such an institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an alternate path to micro entity status distinct from the (a) requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro entity — filing/payment timing and continuity rules (e),(f),(g)
rubrics_metrics.description: A fee may be paid in the micro entity amount only if submitted with, or subsequent to, submission of a certification of entitlement to micro entity status. A certification need only be filed once in an application or patent and, once established, remains in effect until changed pursuant to § 1.29(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if certification was filed, the micro entity status must be appropriate on the date each fee is paid. A second certification is not required if assignment/obligation to micro entities occurs after filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro entity — determination and Office reliance (h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to submitting a micro entity certification, a determination should be made that each applicant qualifies under paragraph (a) or (d) and that any other party holding rights qualifies for small entity status under § 1.27. The Office will generally not question certifications made in accordance with the requirements of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are expected to make reasonable determinations; the Office typically will not challenge properly made certifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro entity — notification of loss of entitlement (i)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notification of a loss of entitlement to micro entity status must be filed in the application or patent prior to paying, or at the time of paying, any fee after the date on which micro entity status is no longer appropriate. The notification must be signed by a party identified in § 1.33(b). Payment of a fee in other than the micro entity amount is not sufficient notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A notification of loss of micro entity status is not treated as a notification of loss of small entity status unless it also contains notification under § 1.27(f)(2). Once filed, regaining micro entity status requires a new certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micro entity — fraud and good faith error relief (j),(k)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attempting to fraudulently establish or pay fees as a micro entity is considered fraud on the Office. If micro entity status and payments were established/paid in good faith but later discovered to be in error, the error may be excused upon compliance with itemization and deficiency payment requirements of paragraph (k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (k) requires separate papers limited to the deficiency payment for a single application/patent, itemization of fees erroneously paid, the micro entity fee actually paid and dates, calculation of deficiency owed (difference between correct fee at date of payment and micro fee), and that failure to comply may lead to processing fees or return of payment. Submission of a deficiency payment will be treated as notification of loss of entitlement under (i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of attorney — definition and basic formality requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Power of attorney means a written document by which a principal authorizes one or more patent practitioners or joint inventors to act on the principal’s behalf. A power of attorney must be in writing, name one or more representatives in compliance with § 1.32(c), give the representative power to act on behalf of the principal, and be signed by the applicant for patent or the patent owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A juristic entity applicant (e.g., organizational assignee) must be represented by a patent practitioner. Specific signature rules and who may sign vary in cross-referenced sections (§§ 1.42, 3.71, 3.73).

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of attorney — who may be named as representative (limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: A power of attorney may only name as representative: (1) one or more joint inventors, (2) those registered patent practitioners associated with a Customer Number, and (3) ten or fewer patent practitioners, stating the name and registration number of each. The Office will not recognize more than ten practitioners of record except as provided in (c)(1) or (c)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more than ten practitioners are named, a separate paper must indicate which ten are to be recognized as of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of attorney — effect of prior application POA in continuing applications (d)
rubrics_metrics.description: A power of attorney from a prior national application for which benefit is claimed may have effect in the continuing application if a copy of the prior power of attorney is filed in the continuing application unless (1) the power of attorney was granted by the inventor, and (2) the continuing application names an inventor who was not named in the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addition of an inventor pursuant to § 1.48 who does not provide a consistent power of attorney results in loss of that prior power upon grant of the § 1.48 request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of attorney — revocation (§ 1.36(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A power of attorney may be revoked at any stage in the proceedings by the applicant or patent owner. A power of attorney to practitioners associated with a Customer Number will be treated as a request to revoke any earlier powers of attorney previously given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fewer than all applicants (or owners) may revoke only upon a showing of sufficient cause and payment of the petition fee (§ 1.17(f)). The Office will notify the patent practitioner(s) of the revocation; notices are mailed to the correspondence address in effect before revocation. Assignment by itself does not operate as a revocation, though the assignee may revoke and grant a new power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of practitioner of record (§ 1.36(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered patent attorney or patent agent given a power of attorney may withdraw as attorney or agent of record upon application to and approval by the Director. The applicant or patent owner will be notified of the withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deletion of all practitioners associated with a Customer Number may not be granted if an Office action requiring a reply is outstanding and insufficient time remains to file a reply. See § 41.5 for PTAB withdrawal procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer Number usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Customer Number may be used to designate the correspondence address for an application or patent, designate the fee address (§ 1.363), and submit a list of patent practitioners such that those practitioners associated with the Customer Number would have power of attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more than one correspondence address is specified, the Office may select the address associated with a Customer Number over a typed correspondence address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence address requirement and communication direction (§ 1.33(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing an application, a correspondence address must be set forth in an application data sheet (§ 1.76) or elsewhere in a clearly identifiable manner in any paper submitted with the application filing. If no correspondence address is specified, the Office may treat the mailing address of the first named inventor (if provided) as the correspondence address. The Office will direct all notices and communications to the person associated with the correspondence address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For correspondence submitted via the electronic filing system, an electronic acknowledgment will be sent to the submitter. The Office will generally not engage in double correspondence with applicant and practitioner except as necessary. A daytime telephone number should be supplied and may be changed by parties authorized to change correspondence address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may sign amendments and other papers (§ 1.33(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments and other papers filed in the application must be signed by: (1) a patent practitioner of record; (2) a patent practitioner not of record who acts in a representative capacity under § 1.34; or (3) the applicant. Unless otherwise specified, papers on behalf of a juristic entity must be signed by a patent practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain written assertions under § 1.27 have separate signing rules; see cross-references for exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence address change and use for maintenance fees (§ 1.33(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'correspondence address' or change thereto may be filed during the enforceable life of the patent. The 'correspondence address' will be used in any correspondence relating to the application and will be used for maintenance fee correspondence unless a separate 'fee address' has been specified (§ 1.363).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A change of address filed in an application or patent does not change the address for a patent practitioner in the roster of attorneys and agents (§ 11.11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acting in a representative capacity — signature and registration requirement (§ 1.34)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent practitioner acting in a representative capacity appears in person or signs a paper, the appearance or signature constitutes a representation to the Office that he or she is authorized to represent the party. The practitioner must set forth his or her registration number, name and signature. Further proof of authority may be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the practitioner's attestation of authority when signing while not of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence address change in continuing applications (§ 1.33(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where application papers from a prior application are used in a continuing application and the correspondence address was changed during prosecution of the prior application, an application data sheet or separate paper identifying the correspondence address to be used for the continuing application must be submitted; otherwise the Office may not recognize the change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures continuity of the intended correspondence address in continuing filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship — requirement to include inventor name(s) (§ 1.41(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application must include, or be amended to include, the name of the inventor for any invention claimed in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is applicable for nonprovisional applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) or 363 on or after Sept. 16, 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship determination for nonprovisional applications (§ 1.41(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventorship of a nonprovisional application is the inventor or joint inventors set forth in the application data sheet in accordance with § 1.76 filed before or concurrently with the inventor’s oath or declaration. If an ADS is not filed before or concurrently with the oath/declaration, inventorship is as set forth in the oath/declaration (subject to § 1.53(d)(4) and § 1.63(d)). Corrections of inventorship must be pursuant to § 1.48 after an ADS or oath/declaration is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If neither an ADS nor an oath/declaration is filed, inventorship is determined from application papers filed pursuant to § 1.53(b) unless applicant supplies inventor names with the processing fee in § 1.17(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship for provisional applications (§ 1.41(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventorship of a provisional application is the inventor or joint inventors set forth in the cover sheet as prescribed by § 1.51(c)(1). Once that cover sheet is filed, any correction of inventorship must be pursuant to § 1.48. If the cover sheet is not filed, inventorship is the inventor(s) set forth in application papers filed under § 1.53(c) unless applicant supplies inventor names with the processing fee in § 1.17(q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the procedural vehicle (cover sheet) for naming inventors in provisional filings and how to correct inventorship thereafter.
